title: He sold his own auto-rickshaw for a shot at a medal. He won it. September 27, 2026.
excerpt: From a studio that outlived its founder to a railway built for cargo alone, September 27's five stories share one thread: the biggest wins came from giving something up first - comfort, ownership, a means of income, a decade of nominations without a win.
bodyHtml:
Every story today involved a real sacrifice before the payoff - a company built from nothing, an income given up for a shot at something bigger, a decade of trying without winning, and infrastructure that took giving up mixed-use tracks to finally move faster.

September 27, 1932: a studio built from nothing outlived the man who built it

Yash Chopra was born on September 27, 1932, in Lahore, British India. His 1965 film 'Waqt' became his breakthrough, and in 1970 he founded Yash Raj Films, now one of Bollywood's most influential studios. His films with Sridevi and later Shah Rukh Khan shifted Hindi cinema toward romance as a genre in its own right. He won 6 National Film Awards, 8 Filmfare Awards, the Dadasaheb Phalke Award, the Padma Bhushan, and in 2006 became the first Indian given lifetime membership by the British Academy of Film and Television Arts.

He built an AI company from scratch. Jeff Bezos backed it. Forbes now values him at $2.1 billion

Aravind Srinivas, co-founder and CEO of Perplexity, holds a Bachelor's and Master's from IIT Madras and a PhD from UC Berkeley, with earlier research stints at OpenAI and Google DeepMind. He co-founded the AI search company in August 2022. Perplexity's valuation climbed from $520 million in January 2024 to $20 billion by late 2025, backed by investors including Jeff Bezos and Google's chief scientist Jeff Dean. As of September 2026, Forbes puts his net worth at $2.1 billion.

He sold his own auto-rickshaw for a shot at a medal. He won it

Jhandu Kumar was born with polio in Harnaut, Bihar, the son of a vegetable vendor. He helped sell vegetables and later drove an auto-rickshaw to support his family. In 2023, he sold that vehicle to fund a trip to the national para powerlifting championships. At the Commonwealth Games 2026 in Glasgow, he won bronze in men's heavyweight para powerlifting - India's first medal of the Games.

Thirteen Grammy nominations. Still finding new rooms to fill

Anoushka Shankar earned her 12th and 13th Grammy nominations at the 2026 ceremony, for Best Global Music Album and Best Global Music Performance. Born in London to sitar legend Ravi Shankar, she performed alongside her father until his death in 2012, and was the first Indian woman ever nominated for a Grammy and the first to perform live or present at the ceremony.

2,843 kilometres, built for one job: cargo

On September 8, 2026, Prime Minister Modi dedicated the final sections of the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor, making the full 2,843-km Eastern and Western network operational. Days after opening, the Western corridor set a new record - 431 trains interchanged in a single day, breaking its own record from two weeks earlier.

Five stories, one thread: a studio that had to be built before it could outlive its founder, a fortune that came after a company earned its own valuation from scratch, a medal that cost an auto-rickshaw before it paid off, thirteen nominations that arrived one at a time with no guarantee of a fourteenth, and a railway that had to give up mixed traffic to finally move at its own speed. Nothing here arrived free. Everything arrived because something else was given up first.
